judged_text: The findFirst-then-update-else-create sequence is not atomic and no uniqueness constraint is enforced on (userId, appId) here, so concurrent or retried webhook deliveries for the same user+app can create duplicate credentials. Duplicate credential rows for the same user+app make later findFirst results nondeterministic, so bookings can run against a stale token while the fresh one sits unused.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), credentials are modified via a `findFirst` on `{ userId, appId: appMetadata.slug }` followed by either `update` or `create`. This read-then-write sequence is not atomic and is not wrapped in a transaction; concurrent/retried webhook calls can both observe “no credential” and both execute `credential.create`, producing duplicates. The use of `findFirst` (not `findUnique`) plus the inline comment “Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id of the credential” suggests there is no usable uniqueness key for an upsert here, making duplicates a realistic outcome and later `findFirst` results nondeterministic.
